title: Aria object and enemy sprites, boxes and stats
limitations: The native C11 rebuild task exports 574 traced door, enemy, skill and shared-effect sequences, 1,855 indexed frames, 1,199 unique BMPs, frame boxes, anchors, probes (including the shared throw routine's 0x084F1388 and 0x084F139C tables), volleys and all 113 enemy stat records; all 1,200 runtime files are guarded by recorded digests. Coverage remains partial because only objects, skills and enemies whose routines are traced are catalogued. The Python object writer is removed. The enemy-stats table (schema v3) also exports each record's experience (u16 at 0x10) and drop fields (items at 0x08/0x0A, rates at 0x15/0x16, soul rarity, type and index at 0x12/0x17/0x18), which the runtime uses on defeat, metadata/money.tsv the money pickup table 0x085250E4, and metadata/equipment.tsv the weapon and armor records.

title: Aria constructor-table enemy batch (Skeleton through Winged Skeleton)
limitations: Ten native enemy identities now load their traced sheets, palettes, frame boxes and constructor states; only first observable patrol, swim, hover and homing loops are connected. Multipart children, attacks, probes, fades, sounds and rewards remain open.

title: Aria Peeping Eye and White Dragon linked children
limitations: Peeping Eye emits its two overlays and six linked static frames; White Dragon emits all nine animation-1 body parts in linked batches. Native polar/affine choreography, attack callbacks, fades, sounds and rewards remain open.

title: Aria early-enemy motion controller wiring
limitations: Dedicated parent motion controllers now dispatch Peeping Eye, White Dragon, Buer, Rock Armor, Giant Ghost and Winged Skeleton movement. Native polar/affine choreography, probes, attacks, fades, sounds and rewards remain open.

title: Aria Peeping Eye polar and White Dragon articulated motion
limitations: Peeping Eye segments target Soma with fixed-point polar offsets; White Dragon parts follow a curved linked chain and forward per-part angles to the renderer. Full attack timing, probes, affine scale/matrix details, damage callbacks, fades, sounds and rewards remain open.

title: Aria White Dragon central affine slot
limitations: The middle linked record uses the traced shared unit-scale affine slot and angle. White Dragon state-3 recovery now lasts 30 frames and returns the head to idle on update 31, ROM-free tested. Full attacks, palette matrices, hit forwarding, death, SFX and yellow soul ability remain incomplete.

title: Aria Peeping Eye attack entry and polar envelope
limitations: The native 180 by 200 activation window starts a visual wind-up, extension and retraction of the linked polar tendrils. The ROM variant table, exact timing, probes, damage callbacks, fades, sounds and rewards remain open.

title: Aria Peeping Eye timed entry sequence
limitations: The Peeping Eye now runs its traced ten-stage, 40-frame polar extension sequence after its native activation gate. Random target selection, the state-3 variant branch table, probes, damage callbacks, fades, sounds and rewards remain open.

title: Aria Peeping Eye random target steering
limitations: The Peeping Eye's 64..112-pixel random sideways and 32..80-pixel upward targets now consume exactly three RNG values. Its steering uses symmetric +/-0x800 acceleration with 31/32 damping, a two-pixel-per-frame velocity cap, a fresh 120-frame timeout and preserved height between targets. The ROM visual variant table, ceiling probes, hit callbacks, fades, sounds and reward parity remain incomplete.

title: Aria Bone Pillar and Buer linked components
limitations: Bone Pillar now assembles its native 22-pixel linked tower and Buer emits its linked second direct frame. Per-segment and fire collision, bounce timing, attacks, fades, sounds and rewards remain open. Buer's separate native state-4 updater now raises the inert visual once by 32 pixels and advances its 0x100 orbit phase; the emitted effect remains missing. Buer's lethal state-3 dispatch now runs the native 96/128-frame death counters with 0x6E sound requests. The linked death effect and eight fragments remain absent. Buer state 2 now preserves the GBA 0xFF wait threshold and 32..63-frame RNG window/retry timing; linked motion and effects remain open. Buer state-2 proximity now starts its native 80-frame attack/32-frame recovery cycle and requests 0x84 at the source-derived frame values. Linked projectile visuals and motion still need dedicated ports. Buer's linked fire sprite now preserves its own facing bit and the source-derived one-flip-per-window timing, with correct parent velocity direction on idle restart. Native flame attacks and linked sprite effects remain incomplete.

title: Aria file selection and runtime launch bridge
limitations: The SDL host runs the native boot, title, main-menu and introduction controllers, maps typed file operations onto three checksummed portable files and one-use quicksave companions, and launches the room runtime only after the native gameplay handoff. With --rom it verifies the user's Aria image, renders all five native main-menu background layouts in three languages, and renders the introduction's language banks, proportional font, palette, character banks and scrolling block maps directly from memory without exporting ROM bytes. Portable schema v9 preserves runtime progression, inventory, souls, action buttons, bestiary discoveries and common/rare drop discoveries. Dynamic menu entity/OAM text, file statistics, cursor art and native title artwork remain absent, as do the introduction actors' OAM, animation frames, affine transforms and alpha composition. Completed-file metadata, events and map state remain open; portable quicksaves use companion files instead of native SRAM.

title: Aria native save-room detection and portable checkpoint writes
limitations: The native room exporter carries the global-map save/warp bits in schema v4, while runtime v3 exports remain compatible and detect object 0x1C. Up inside the native Object1C rectangle restores HP and writes a schema-v9 snapshot of room, spawn, vitals, movement, progression, equipment, inventories, souls, button configuration, bestiary and common/rare drop discoveries to the selected portable slot. Native healing animation, Yes/No prompt, object art, event/map state and SRAM parity remain open.

title: Aria runtime rooms (background, video memory, BG1 collision, transitions, entities)
limitations: The native importer was source-compared on 342 BG1 collision maps, complete VRAM/palette snapshots for all 343 rooms, 901 expanded static tilemaps and 150929408 rendered RGBA pixels, 342 static-origin RGB composites totaling 61210624 pixels and their byte-identical 183650340-byte BMP representation, plus 342 byte-identical AOSROOM-NATIVE v4 payloads totaling 2035730 bytes with 956416 cells, 725 transitions and 2335 entities. Its atomic writer produces the same 685 private files as the former Python exporter, including the SHA-256 index, and now runs the aria_rooms rebuild task alone; recorded SHA-256 digests guard every native command, both catalog files and every export file. One room has no BG1 payload. The editor previews use the separate native renderer of src/editor_backend/aria_render.c, byte-identical to the removed Python renderer on all 343 rooms.

title: Soma animation library
limitations: The native C11 rebuild task exports all 83 Soma animations and the one supported knife animation as 382 indexed frames and 152 unique BMPs; all 155 files are byte-identical to the former Python writer and guarded by recorded digests. Animation-specific palette banks are preserved. Knife animation 1 still has unsupported multi-component OAM. The Python writer and its unconsumed preview decoder are removed.

title: Soma weapon records and blade sprites
limitations: The native C11 rebuild task exports all 59 weapon records plus the unarmed record, 60 sprite sequences, 416 indexed frames, 255 unique BMPs and both metadata tables; all 258 files are byte-identical to the former Python writer and guarded by recorded digests. Class 1 blades rotate about the entity position (the affine double-size placement is not modelled), and the class 4 casing and impact come from the object library. The Python weapon writer is removed.

title: Music and sound effects
limitations: Zero Mission: its sound bank and engine tables are exported privately; the music and the sound effects of the ported systems (Samus, weapons, hatches, blocks, enemies, drops) play through the ported engine, with the item jingles inserted in front of the music and the current track replayed after them, and the Chozo hint music; the audio device pulls the sound frame by frame at the hardware's 65.536 kHz rate (resampled by SDL), so game slowdowns cannot starve it; not yet compared with hardware. Liquids, ground effects, charge beams, bombs and bosses have no sounds yet. Aria: the native aria_sound task exports all 495 gSongTable records and fixed MP2K header fields into a private golden-guarded manifest. The runtime loads the real player and priority metadata before PlaySong and advances the StartSong, AudioCommand and volume-ramp controller each lifecycle frame. A bounded standalone track decoder now handles the native wait table, running status, notes, parameters, branches, patterns and repeats, but it is not yet connected to the private bank or StartSong. Voice allocation, samples, mixing and SDL output are absent, so requests remain inaudible.

The native C11 metroid_sprites rebuild task writes all 20,088 sequences, 117,235 frames and 27,806 unique BMPs, the OAM bounds and sprites.tsv, byte-identical to the former Python writer; the ported sprites' tables are a generated copy of the pinned decompilation and recorded digests guard the index, bounds, tables and object names.

limitations: The C11 library verifies both ROMs and writes their exact private identity manifests atomically; reproduces Aria's structural catalog, BG1 collision, complete room VRAM/palettes, 901 background tilemaps, exact 4-bpp RGBA renders, 342 static-origin room composites, exact BMP serialization and 342 exact AOSROOM-NATIVE v4 payloads, writes the complete 685-file private room export, writes all 155 Soma/knife, 258 weapon and 1,187 traced-object library files atomically, and exports all 495 gSongTable records with the fixed fields of their MP2K headers; reproduces Zero Mission's ROM bank and symbol manifest; and decodes all 331 Zero Mission room descriptors, Clipdata maps, every BG0-BG3 payload, all 79 standard tileset VRAM/palette snapshots, complete metatile tables, 1115 exact RGBA room layers, 330 exact background selections with byte-identical BMP/mask serialization, 330 exact complete MVROOM-NATIVE payloads through the U/L/E/G/R/T metadata and P/S/F/J/N sprite records, the exact BMP32 tileset sheets and text layers of the room export, its exact blocks.tsv and power_bomb.tsv tables and background.bmp images, and writes that complete export with its SHA-256 index atomically. Both identity manifests, the Aria world catalog, Soma, weapon, object and song-table libraries, the Zero Mission ROM bank and both room exports run natively in the rebuild task graph, as do the Zero Mission sound bank, sprites and raw import; no Python extractor remains.
